newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb, rebel Serbs reach deals on reunification.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb, rebel Serbs reach deals on reunification.

text.p: Croatia and rebel minority Serbs in eastern Slavonia signed several agreements on Wednesday to smooth the region's return to Zagreb's rule, moving a step closer to peace.
"A number of constructive agreements have been reached," U.S. General Jacques Klein told reporters after a meeting between Croatian and Serb officials in Zagreb.
Klein heads the U.N. Transitional Administration for Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES). Its 5,000 peacekeepers oversee the region's gradual reintegration into Croatia, from which it broke away in 1991.
"People in the region are ready for a change. They want a better future...and what was done today will, I think, ensure that future," Klein said.
The sides agreed to reopen a railway line between the government-held town of Vinkovci and the Serb eastern outpost of Sid, and to start registering local Serb companies, Klein said.
Croatian Deputy Prime Minister Ivica Kostovic, who took part in the talks, said a draft agreement was also reached for a special school curriculum for the region's Serb minority.
They further agreed to increase the number of government offices in Eastern Slavonia which issue citizenship papers to local Serbs.
Elections for the area's local administration are due to be held next year, before the UNTAES mandate expires. Voters must posess valid Croatian papers to vote.
Local Serbs claim the area became home to some 60,000 Serbs from two other rebel enclaves, which Zagreb troops recaptured last year. Kostovic estimates the number closer to 22,000.
"We need those (paper-issuing) offices quickly to know how many people live in the area, if we're going to have election in a timely manner," he said.
